rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods / Table 4 - two-year field experiment (2012-2013) at Bainijing, Inner Mongolia, with five drip fertigation levels in a randomized block design with three replicates, reporting own tuber yield, IWP and PFP data.
rows.notes: All plots were drip-fertigated; the treatment variable is fertilizer dose, not irrigation method. The study reports irrigation amounts (92-173 mm) and IWP by fertigation level, but never compares drip with another irrigation method, nor measures evaporation, runoff or water savings. The only comparison with local LEPA enterprises concerns yield, not water use. So it offers no result of its own on drip irrigation conserving water or minimizing evaporation/runoff; its evidence is about the optimal fertigation dose (72% NPK) under SMP-based drip scheduling.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods / Table 4 - own two-year field experiment on sandy and loamy sand soil comparing five drip fertigation levels for potato, reporting yield, IWP and PFP.
rows.notes: The study is on sandy soil and uses drip, but it does not test drip against traditional irrigation methods and does not measure evaporation, runoff, percolation or water wastage. Statements about sandy soils being prone to leaching and about LEPA come from the introduction and cited literature, not from its own results. Its own results concern fertigation dose effects on yield, IWP and PFP under drip, so it provides no evidence on drip reducing water wastage in sandy soils.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Study is a fertigation-level trial under drip on sandy soil; it contains no comparison of irrigation technologies and no measurement of evaporation or runoff, so it cannot support the water-conservation claims attributed to it.
